To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the spatial distribution of soil salt content in a gravel–sands mulched orchard can be predicted by using inverse distance weighting (b) the temporal distribution can be modeled by using autoregressive moving average (c) the soil salt content in deep layers can be estimated from surface data and (d) a few sampling points are representative of the mean salt content of the field, thus increasing sampling efficiency and decreasing cost.

IDW is the best method to model the spatiotemporally stable spatial variability of soil salt in a gravel–sandy mulched field, that a representative point can be used to estimate the overall salt content in the field, and that the monitoring of soil salt can be simplified by sampling only a few representative points.

the IDW interpolation was the more accurate method to estimate soil salt content in the deeper layers of gravel–sand-mulled jujube orchards, that ARMA was a suitable method for monitoring the spatiotemoral variability of soil salt content, that the spatial patterns of soil salt content were temporally stable, and that a few representative points can be used for monitoring the soil salt content of the entire orchard, thus increasing sampling efficiency and reducing costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatiotemporally dynamic nature of soil salinity and its implications for monitoring and management.
the spatiotemporality of soil salt in a gravel– sand-mulched field, and the results are expected to be of value for researchers and practitioners.
a new method for predicting soil salinity in gravel–sand–mulched jujube fields, which will help to improve the management of soil salinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IDW interpolation was better than cokriged for the estimation of soil salt content in deep layers from surface data; ARMA was accurate for predicting salt content in a time series; and, the monitoring of soil salt content from a few representative locations could be an efficient and cost-saving method to estimate the overall salt content of the field.
IDW and ARMA are the best methods to predict spatial and temporal variability of soil salt content, respectively, in gravel–sand munched jujube orchards.
IDW was the most accurate method of predicting salinity in the deep layers from surface measurements, and the ARMA model was the most appropriate for predicting temporal variability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can predict the soil salinity in gravel–sand fields by using the ARMA time series model and we can identify a location where the soil salt content is representative of the whole field, so that the cost of monitoring soil salt can be reduced.
the IDW interpolation method is more accurate than the cokriging method when using surface salt contents to estimate the content of deep layers.
the IDW interpolation was a more accurate method than cokriged for predicting salinity content in deep soil layers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a few observations are enough to monitor salinity and to predict the overall salt content of a mulched field.
the monitoring of soil salt in deep soil layers can be reduced from the current practice of sampling every 10 cm to a single sampling point, with a mean relative error of 2%.

, in the context of soil monitoring, the use of a single representative location is a valuable tool for reducing the number of samples required to characterize the soil salt in gravel-sand mulched fields.
